page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supporting 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng tests. However, multi-core CPU scaling is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% on stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only operations on both small and large blocks scoring in the bottom 25%, though large block write bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks maintain average performance.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highmem-4 is its high memory capacity paired with modest multi-core compute and memory throughput. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without intensive parallel processing demands. It is suitable for memory-bound applications, text processing, single-threaded data compression, and lightweight database operations that fit within its memory footprint.
